title: Transforming Teacher Education in Developing Countries: The Role of Generative AI in Bridging Theory and Practice
extended_summary:
This paper is a perspective/theoretical study about how generative AI (GenAI) could address longstanding problems in teacher education in developing countries, using Ghana as the main case. The central problem is the persistent gap between theory-heavy teacher preparation and the limited implementation of pedagogical modeling and performance-based assessment in initial teacher education programs.

Rather than reporting an empirical intervention, the paper argues that GenAI can reduce the burden of content delivery and content knowledge acquisition, allowing teacher educators to spend more time on modeling teaching practices, supporting authentic assessment, and strengthening professional development. The author also suggests that GenAI may help reduce resistance to curricular change, improve access to resources, and encourage digital literacy and critical thinking among pre-service teachers.

The context is Ghanaian initial teacher education, especially the four-year colleges of education reform and its constructivist/experiential orientation. The paper concludes that GenAI could catalyze broader systemic change in teacher education and, downstream, improve K-12 teaching and workforce readiness, but it warns about misuse and the possible erosion of critical thinking and creativity. It calls for scaffolded GenAI literacy and future empirical research on responsible integration.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative artificial intelligence / large language model tools used for content synthesis, drafting, feedback, and instructional support.
identified_tools.use_case: This is a perspective/theoretical paper arguing that generative AI could support teacher education in developing countries by reducing content-delivery burden, enabling pedagogical modeling, supporting performance-based assessment, and aiding professional development; it does not evaluate a specific deployed product in an intervention.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a perspective/theoretical paper using logical deduction and literature citation rather than an empirical controlled or quasi-controlled evaluation. It does not report original outcome data, subgroup analyses, or moderation findings.
impact_tier_rationale: Because no empirical effects are reported, there is no measurable impact estimate to classify as positive or negative. The paper argues for potentially substantial system-level influence, but this remains speculative rather than demonstrated.
